title: Stream gateway observability handoff and OTEL span affix
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: implement a Stream Gateway component that performs deterministic observability handoff for structured log events and attaches OpenTelemetry (OTEL) span/trace anchors before forwarding to downstream sinks (Loki/Elastic). This ticket scopes the gateway adapter, the minimal schema-catalog enforcement layer, and a backfill plan for existing JSONL producers.

Problem statement: multiple producers emit a mix of legacy JSONL, partially-structured events, and fully-structured logs. Correlation is unreliable because spans are created client-side inconsistently and trace IDs are sometimes missing or duplicated. Downstream dashboards (latency/error) suffer from missing span relationships and high-cardinality fields due to ad-hoc key names.

Proposed solution: build a high-throughput stream gateway service that sits between Kafka intake topics and our enrichment tier. Responsibilities: canonicalize fields using a schema-catalog lookup (field aliases -> canonical keys), inject/normalize a tenant-scoped correlation ID when absent, attach an OTEL span context header using our trace fingerprint algorithm (deterministic from request_id/service/ts when no upstream span), and emit both enriched structured log and OTEL-link metadata for Loki and ES pipeline consumers.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change SDKs or client instrumentation. We'll provide a compatibility shim for producers in a follow-up.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stream Gateway accepts JSONL and structured events at sustained 15k eps (peak 50k eps burst) with p99 < 250ms processing overhead (measured in staging).
- Canonical schema mapping applied per schema-catalog rules; unknown fields preserved under "extra" namespace.
- If no trace/span is present, gateway generates OTEL span context deterministically and emits trace.parent/span in both event and OTEL metadata header.
- Downstream Loki pipeline receives events with stable correlation_id and trace_id 99% of the time for sampled traffic.
- Backfill job plan documented and a safe runbook for reprocessing 7 days of logs without duplicate indices in ES or duplicate frames in Loki.
- Unit and integration tests for schema mapping, idempotency, and span-generation.

Implementation notes:
- Ingest source: kafka topic telemetry-raw (partitioned by tenant_id).
- Use a stateless gateway behind an autoscaling k8s HPA with CPU-based scaling and a request-based buffer for bursts.
- Transform functions implemented in Rust for low latency; use existing kv-cache service for schema-catalog lookups with TTL 15s.
- Emit two downstream topics: telemetry-enriched (for enrichment and KV cache consumers) and telemetry-observability (OTEL+Loki/ES shapes).
- Backfill approach: streaming Replayer job that reads from raw-archive S3 keys, applies the gateway transforms in a dry-run mode to validate, then writes to a deduping write path to ES/Loki sink.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Adding deterministic span generation may create synthetic traces that could be misinterpreted by customers; we'll tag generated spans with origin=generated and include deterministic_seed details.
- Inline schema enforcement may increase processing overhead; mitigated by a fast in-memory alias map and health checks to fall back to passthrough mode if latency rises.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy gateway in staging with passthrough + logging enabled.
2) Canary 10% of telemetry-raw -> telemetry-enriched (internal tenants) for 48hrs, monitor error/latency dashboards and trace continuity.
3) Enable full mapping and span-affix for low-volume tenants for 7 days.
4) Gradually onboard higher-volume tenants.

Telemetry to monitor during rollout: p50/p95/p99 processing overhead, error rate (transform failures), fraction of events with correlation_id, fraction with generated spans, Loki ingestion success rate, ES index duplicate count.
comments: 2026-01-21 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Agreed to reuse kv-cache service for alias lookups. Action: Diego to prototype span-generation module.

2026-01-26 - Diego Morales: Prototype complete (rust). Measured ~120us per event for alias lookup + span affix on small dataset. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/2198 (WIP)

2026-01-28 - Priya Nambiar (Observability PM): Reviewed prototype. Concern: synthetic spans could inflate trace counts in retention billing. Suggest sampling and explicit tag for generated spans. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-01-30 - Security review (initial): No PII extraction observed in transforms. Confirmed that tenant_id mapping must be treated as sensitive when surfaced to logs. Security flagged that any debug dumps must be redacted. (Follow-up: add redaction pass.)

2026-02-01 - Diego Morales: Implemented sampling and origin=generated tag; added redaction layer for debug output. Bench run: sustained 18k eps on t3-large equivalent (staging), p99 processing overhead 210ms with warm kv-cache. Added integration tests for idempotent backfill path.

2026-02-02 - QA: Ran canary dry-run for internal-telemetry tenant. No duplicate indices observed in ES write path; Loki pipeline metrics show 0.2% increase in error frames (investigating). Next: enable detailed logs for affected partitions and run backfill dry-run for 72 hours.
